claims.text: Adaptive bias force or metadynamics should be implemented for free-energy calculations in multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The proposed advanced sampling technique will substantially reduce the cost of obtaining fusion properties of high-entropy systems.
The proposed advanced sampling technique will substantially reduce the cost of obtaining high-temperature thermodynamic properties of high-entropy systems.
Adaptive bias force or metadynamics will enhance sampling efficiency in the proposed free-energy calculations.
Enhanced sampling efficiency will reduce computational cost.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 2–5 relative to explicit ab initio molecular-dynamics workflows.
The proposed method will reduce computational cost by a factor of 2–5 relative to TOR-TILD.
The intended composition domain comprises high-entropy systems containing 3–6 elements.
The intended temperature domain is 500–2000 K.
The accuracy of advanced sampling for complex high-entropy systems is uncertain.
The proposed method should be benchmarked against explicit ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD using computational cost and thermodynamic-property accuracy.
Failure to reduce computational cost by at least 20% would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure to reproduce reference thermodynamic properties within 10% would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted 2–5-fold speedup requires at least a 50% cost reduction, whereas the hypothesis is only falsified below a 20% reduction. Thus, a 20–49% reduction would fail the stated prediction but would not falsify the hypothesis.
